nodes.label: NEG minus Typo Flip-Rate Difference Chart
nodes.norm_label: neg minus typo flip-rate difference chart
nodes.rationale: Two-panel grouped bar chart (with error bars, likely 95% CIs) of the difference in prediction flip rate between negation (NEG) perturbations and typo perturbations, on 352 shared ids, across tiers T1-T3 for three multilingual encoders. At T1, NEG flips slightly more than typos (~+2 to +4.5%); at T2 and T3 the difference turns negative and grows (T3 about -6% to -10% for flip), i.e. typos cause more flips than negation at higher intensity. XLM-R is closest to zero / most positive throughout; mBERT shows the largest negative gap at T3 (~-9.5%).

nodes.label: Condition a_typos
nodes.rationale: n_changed_words is the strongest positive predictor (OR ~2.1); margin_A strongly negative (~0.48); n_words_A negative (~0.75); model terms near 1.

nodes.label: Condition b_typos_case_emoji
nodes.rationale: Tightest CIs (likely largest sample, INFERRED). n_changed_words (~1.6), delta_fertility (~1.3), char_edit_dist_ci (~1.2) positive; margin_A strongly negative (~0.40); n_words_A ~0.78; model terms near 1.

nodes.label: Condition c_D_only
nodes.rationale: Only condition where model identity matters: MuRIL (~0.38) and XLM-R (~0.45) have much lower odds than the reference model (reference not shown; possibly mBERT, AMBIGUOUS). delta_fertility positive (~1.2); most other CIs cross 1; margin_A effect weak (~0.9).

nodes.label: delta_fertility
nodes.rationale: Only predictor significantly >1 in all three conditions: increased tokenizer fertility under perturbation raises outcome odds.

nodes.label: margin_A
nodes.rationale: Strongest protective factor: higher original-prediction confidence margin sharply lowers outcome odds (OR ~0.4-0.5 in a and b).

nodes.label: unk_rate
nodes.rationale: Near OR=1 in all conditions: unknown-token rate does not predict the outcome.

nodes.label: Regression Odds Ratios Forest Plot
nodes.rationale: Three-panel forest plot of standardized logistic-regression odds ratios (per SD, 95% CI, log x-axis, reference line at OR=1) for predictors of an outcome under three perturbation conditions. Outcome is likely a prediction flip/robustness failure (INFERRED, not labeled).

nodes.norm_label: 95% ci via cluster bootstrap (sentence ids, 3 seeds pooled, 2,000 resamples)

nodes.label: Condition D
nodes.rationale: The most disruptive condition by a wide margin for all three models. Its meaning is not stated in the figure.

nodes.label: Condition NE
nodes.rationale: Barely changes predictions (about 0.5-2%). It can serve as a near-invariance control.

nodes.label: Perturbation Conditions T1, T2, T3, LC, NE, UC, D, NEG
nodes.norm_label: perturbation conditions t1, t2, t3, lc, ne, uc, d, neg
nodes.rationale: AMBIGUOUS: the abbreviations are not defined in the figure. One plausible reading is T1-T3 = transliteration levels, LC/UC = lower/upper case, NE = named entities, D = a script or dropping change, NEG = negation. This reading is not confirmed.

nodes.label: Flip Rate vs A
nodes.rationale: Share of items whose prediction changes relative to condition A. Approximate readings: T1 ~7%, T2 ~12-14%, T3 ~18-19%, LC ~8-11%, NE ~1-2%, UC ~11-13%, D mBERT ~58% / XLM-R ~34% / MuRIL ~29%, NEG ~9-13%.

nodes.label: bert-base-multilingual-cased
nodes.rationale: Most fragile under condition D: about 58% flips, and about 62% strict flips.

nodes.label: muril-base-cased
nodes.rationale: Lowest flip rate under D and the lowest seed-disagreement baseline (~12.8%). It may be the most robust model on code-mixed input.

nodes.label: Seed Disagreement on A (dotted baseline)
nodes.rationale: How often different training seeds disagree on condition A, labelled as a different quantity from the flip rate. It works as a noise reference. Approximate values: XLM-R ~18.5%, mBERT ~17.8%, MuRIL ~12.8%. Only condition D, and T3 for MuRIL, clearly go above the model's own seed noise.

nodes.label: Strict Flip Rate (A prediction correct)
nodes.rationale: Flip rate restricted to items where the A prediction was correct, so it isolates cases where a correct answer is broken. The pattern matches the top panel. Approximate D values: mBERT ~62%, XLM-R ~28%, MuRIL ~25.5%. All other conditions stay at or below ~16%.

nodes.label: xlm-roberta-base
nodes.rationale: Highest flip rates under NE and NEG, and the highest seed-disagreement baseline.

nodes.label: Flip Rates Figure (flip rate vs A and strict flip rate by condition and model)
nodes.norm_label: flip rates figure (flip rate vs a and strict flip rate by condition and model)
nodes.rationale: Two-panel grouped bar chart. It compares how often each model's prediction flips from condition A under 8 conditions (T1, T2, T3, LC, NE, UC, D, NEG). Condition D causes by far the most flips, and mBERT is the least robust there.
